question.worked_solution:
The variable $x$ is being *multiplied* by $-5.$ To isolate $x,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-5.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5x\,\, & <\,\,10 \\ \frac{-5x}{-5}\,\, & >\,\,\frac{10}{-5} \\ \frac{-5x}{-5}\,\, & >\,\,-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-5$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-5x}{-5} & >-2 \\ \frac{\cancel{-5}x}{\cancel{-5}} & >-2 \\ x & >-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x>-2.$
